I'm a 33-year-old farmer in Quzhou, been at this for 5 years now. Middle school education, but I've learned plenty from extension trainings and watching what my neighbors do—especially Old Wang down the road with his 200 mu, he's always trying new things. I manage 163 mu, which is big enough that I have to think like a business, not just a smallholder. My household has four people, but my wife works at the garment factory in town and my father's getting older, so family labor is tight. I hire workers for the busy seasons and rent machinery for tillage and harvest.

Right now it's March, so the wheat I planted last October on 100 mu is waking up. I'm planning to topdress soon—extension says 15 kg N per mu, but I usually do 18 because my soil's a bit sandy and I learned that 15 leaves the wheat looking yellow at jointing. I split it: base before planting was already done, now the topdress at jointing. Last year I got 420 kg/mu, hoping for 450 this year if the spring rains cooperate.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll immediately plant summer maize on the same 100 mu. That window is brutal—usually 5 to 7 days. I rent a combine and a corn planter, and hire 10-15 workers. Maize gets hybrid seed at 40 yuan/mu, and I apply 16 kg N total, split between base at planting and side-dress at the 6-leaf stage. I expect around 500 kg/mu if the summer drought doesn't hit too hard.

I keep 30 mu in cotton—it's reliable, less labor than vegetables, and the price has been decent. Planted mid-April, harvested September through October with multiple picks. Two fertilizer applications, base and at flowering. I budget two irrigations for cotton, but I watch the sky.

The vegetables are where the profit is, but they're risky and labor-heavy. Watermelon on 15 mu, planted late March under plastic mulch with drip lines. Needs three irrigations and a lot of potassium. I'm targeting 3000 kg/mu, but I know one bad rain at flowering can ruin it. Broccoli on 10 mu I plant in August for autumn harvest—better market prices then. Chili on 5 mu, standard spring planting. Stevia on 3 mu is my experiment this year—a buyer promised to purchase dried leaves, so I'm testing small. If it pays, I'll expand next year.

Everything runs on well water here, and it's metered and costly. Wheat gets 4 irrigations because it's my main income, maize gets 2, vegetables get more because they need it. Total input budget is about 135,000 yuan this year. That's a big number, but with 163 mu, if you don't put money in, you don't get money out. I learned that the hard way my first year when I tried to save on fertilizer and ended up with yields 20% below my neighbors.
